target: UTM-bundled QEMU, AArch64 PCI, one vCPU, disposable writable RedSea VirtIO fixture
result: pass: FilesFind reports the real RedSea file start sector; stock DiskCheck preserves that file, frees the separate orphan allocation, and returns a clean second scan
verified: The disposable 128-sector writable RedSea volume mounts as D with a valid bounded geometry.
The root directory contains KEEP.ZC, whose first sector is data_area + 9; its allocation bit is set alongside the root directory and a separate orphan cluster.
FilesFind("D:/*", FUF_RECURSE) returns exactly KEEP.ZC with the expected path, physical starting sector, size, and archive attribute.
The ARM64 ZcRedSeaFileAt bridge now returns each file's physical starting sector, and TaskBridge stores it in CDirEntry.clus as stock RedSea DiskCheck expects.
DiskCheck('D', TRUE, FALSE) reports only the independent orphan allocation, frees it, and leaves the KEEP.ZC allocation bit set.
DiskCheck('D', FALSE, FALSE) then returns zero; final zstatus reports failed=0.
limits: The fixture contains one root file; nested populated-directory checking and directory repair remain untested.
This tests a disposable QEMU disk fixture, not physical SD or USB media.
FAT32 repair and live UTM UI or Raspberry Pi behavior are not established.
